subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: Should this be solved by sponsoring the broader tools.fs.roots policy, by adding a narrow media-tool local-root allowlist, or by keeping current channel-scoped roots with no new core config?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent public config surface changes host filesystem access semantics and overlaps an open broad PR, so automation should not choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Unify Under tools.fs.roots
options.body: Use the broader filesystem-root model, or a smaller successor to it, as the single operator-controlled policy for host reads and media loading.

options.title: Add Narrow Media Allowlist
options.body: Expose a dedicated media-tool local-root config with strict absolute non-root validation, docs, and regression tests if maintainers want media isolated from general FS policy.

options.title: Keep Current Roots Only
options.body: Decline new host-root config for now and keep default/workspace plus channel-scoped inbound roots, leaving copying or staging as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Unify Under tools.fs.roots
recommendation.body: Use the broader filesystem-root model, or a smaller successor to it, as the single operator-controlled policy for host reads and media loading.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history places the central media/filesystem policy and config surfaces under this contributor's work, making them the best routing candidate for the policy choice.
